comment: it-brain team registry: the single source of truth for teams, knowledge areas and who owns them. scripts/brain.py reads AREAS from here (and `brain.py route` uses each area's keywords to find every area a question touches), generates .gitlab/CODEOWNERS from it (brain.py codeowners) and CI checks that every area has a folder. Group handles are placeholders until the real GitLab groups exist (docs/it-brain/ROADMAP.md). 'provisional: true' marks an ownership the teams have not confirmed yet.

ocp.name: OpenShift Container Platform team
ocp.serves: the OpenShift fleet: hub, MCE and hosted clusters, UPI clusters, GitOps, GPU nodes, cluster-side storage and networking, OADP; our platform tools (server-scan, Temporal / Redbull Workflows) and, provisionally, Prefect, Airflow, Spark, ECK / Elastic, Solr and MongoDB on Kubernetes and VMs

storage.name: Storage team
storage.serves: arrays and storage services: NetApp ONTAP, Dell PowerMax, PowerFlex, PowerScale (Isilon), Ceph and its S3 gateway, ODF, SMB/CIFS shares, Commvault backup; the CSI drivers jointly with the OCP team

network.name: Network team
network.serves: the data-centre fabric and security edge: Cisco ACI, Palo Alto firewalls (and Panorama), and the network side of storage and cluster connectivity

virtualization.name: Virtualization team
virtualization.serves: hypervisors and VMs: KubeVirt / OpenShift Virtualization, VMware vSphere (vCenter, ESXi, vSAN, NSX) and its automation with PowerShell / PowerCLI, Nutanix AOS / AHV / Prism, VM migration (MTV)

domains.data: data platforms on Kubernetes and VMs

openshift.description: OCP platform behaviour, fleet topology (hub / MCE / hosted / UPI), upgrades, operators

kubernetes.description: upstream Kubernetes behaviour and APIs as they apply to our clusters

hypershift.description: HyperShift hosted control planes, HostedCluster and NodePool

baremetal.description: Metal3, Ironic, BareMetalHost, Agent installs, BMC behaviour

vsphere.description: OpenShift running on vSphere: installer, machine API, vSphere CSI from the cluster side (the VMware platform itself is area vmware)

networking.description: cluster networking: OVN-Kubernetes, Multus, ingress, AKO load balancing, egress from the cluster side

storage.description: cluster-side storage: StorageClasses, PV/PVC behaviour, CSI in general, Portworx

gpu.description: GPU nodes, GPU/Network operators, inference stacks

security.description: certificates, RBAC, compliance, CVEs across the estate

oadp.description: OADP / Velero backup and restore of OpenShift workloads, its S3 targets and CSI snapshots

netapp-ontap.description: NetApp ONTAP clusters: SVMs, volumes, LIFs, export policies, SnapMirror, ONTAP S3

trident.description: NetApp Trident CSI on OpenShift: backends, StorageClasses, snapshots, Trident Protect

dell-powermax.description: Dell PowerMax arrays, Unisphere, and the PowerMax CSI driver (Dell CSM)

dell-powerflex.description: Dell PowerFlex (SDS, SDC on nodes), its gateway, and the PowerFlex CSI driver

dell-powerscale.description: Dell PowerScale (Isilon) OneFS: access zones, NFS/SMB/S3, and the PowerScale CSI driver

ceph.description: Ceph clusters: RADOS, RBD, CephFS, and the RGW S3 object gateway

odf.description: OpenShift Data Foundation (Rook-Ceph, NooBaa / MCG) running on or consumed by our clusters

smb-cifs.description: SMB/CIFS shares (ONTAP, PowerScale, Windows) and the SMB CSI driver

commvault.description: Commvault backup: storage policies, media agents, Kubernetes/OpenShift protection

cisco-aci.description: Cisco ACI fabric: tenants, VRFs, bridge domains, EPGs, contracts, L3Outs, APIC

palo-alto.description: Palo Alto firewalls and Panorama: zones, security and NAT policy, App-ID, HA

vmware.description: the VMware platform itself: vCenter, ESXi, vSAN, NSX (OpenShift-on-vSphere quirks stay in area vsphere)

nutanix.description: Nutanix AOS / AHV / Prism, Nutanix Files and Objects, the Nutanix CSI driver

server-scan.description: server-scan: our platform (team-redbull/server-scan) to discover, inventory and manage bare-metal servers — API, UI, scanners, MCP, deployment

temporal.description: Temporal: the server on the hub and the Redbull Workflows orchestrator built on it (segment, server, provisioning and upgrade workflows, task queues, workers)

prefect.description: Prefect: flows, deployments, work pools and workers, Prefect server on Kubernetes

airflow.description: Apache Airflow on Kubernetes and on VMs: scheduler, executors (Kubernetes / Celery), DAG deployment, metadata DB

spark.description: Apache Spark on Kubernetes (spark-submit, Spark operator) and on VMs/YARN: executors, shuffle, S3/HDFS access

elastic.description: Elastic stack on Kubernetes via ECK (Elasticsearch, Kibana, Fleet) and on VMs: shards, ILM, snapshots, upgrades

solr.description: Apache Solr (SolrCloud) on Kubernetes (Solr operator) and on VMs: ZooKeeper, collections, replicas, backups

mongodb.description: MongoDB on Kubernetes (operator) and on VMs: replica sets, sharding, backups, upgrades

kubevirt.description: KubeVirt / OpenShift Virtualization: VMs on OpenShift — virt components, VM lifecycle, CDI / DataVolumes, VM networking (Multus, bridges, localnet, SR-IOV), live migration, scheduling and performance, MTV migration from VMware, backup, debugging, upgrades

powercli.description: PowerShell and VMware PowerCLI: connecting to vCenter, the object model (cmdlets vs Get-View), inventory and reports, VM / host / datastore / vDS operations, credentials, offline install in the air gap, scripts for OpenShift-on-vSphere and migrations

python.description: Python as we write it for our platform tools: Pydantic models and settings (v2), validation and serialization, the Temporal Python SDK's Pydantic data converter, FastAPI in server-scan

meta.description: the brain itself: tooling, sources, versions, conventions

placeholders.<array>: storage array or ONTAP cluster name
placeholders.<volume>: volume, LUN or file system name
placeholders.<pool>: storage pool / Ceph pool / PowerFlex protection domain
placeholders.<share>: SMB share or NFS export path
